svg.title: I2C multi-controller bus access policies: access delay
svg.text: Access delay per controller: worst case and mean
S1, S2: 3 saturated controllers; S3, S4: 3 Poisson sources with 25 % offered load each (75 % in total)
Tmax = 20 ms, tbuf = 0.78 µs, r = 60 µs (measured), margin = 10 µs, tidle = 10 µs, W = 100 µs
Tmax: 1024 bytes × 9 bit / 800 kbit/s (set 1 Mbit/s) = 11.52 ms + 2.7 ms clock stretching = 14.22 ms, rounded up to 20 ms
bar = worst delay, dark tick = mean; util. = bus utilisation
∞: starved (never gets the bus) or overloaded (queue grows without bound)
Policy 1 = Re-arm and retry (baseline) · Policy 2 = Fixed post-ownership deferral · Policy 3 = Idle-window deferral · Policy 4 = Probe and random backoff
S1 · 3 saturated controllers, m = Tmax = 20 ms
S2 · 3 saturated controllers, m = 0.1 Tmax = 2 ms
S3 · 3 Poisson sources, 25 % offered load each, m = 0.1 Tmax = 2 ms
2500 Tmax = 50 s simulated, ≈ 6264 packets per controller
S4 · 3 Poisson sources, 25 % offered load each, m = Tmax = 20 ms
25000 Tmax = 500 s simulated, ≈ 6301 packets per controller
Access delay: S1, S2 from queueing a packet (end of the controller's previous turn, or t = 0) to the START of the transfer that wins the bus; S3, S4 from the packet's
arrival to that START, including the wait behind the controller's own earlier packets. Packets still waiting at the end of the run count with their wait so far.
Policy 1: C never gets the bus in S1 and S2 (A and B alternate); under Poisson load the highest address C waits longest: worst C 80.0 ms in S3, C 672 ms in S4.
Policy 2: worst 40.0 ms = 2.00 Tmax in S1 = 2 Tmax + 3·tbuf. In S3 a controller can use at most m / (m + Tmax + margin) = 9.1 % of bus time < 25 % offered: 3 of 3
queues grow without bound (3985, 4031, 3961 packets waiting after 50 s). S4 stays stable (capacity 50.0 %), but the deferral raises the mean delay to 45.6, 43.8,
Policy 3: worst 40.0 ms = 2.00 Tmax in S1 = 2 Tmax + 2·tbuf + tidle, 4.01 ms in S2, 46.6 ms in S3 and 407 ms in S4. Under Poisson load (S3 and S4) 2 Tmax + tidle does
not bound these delays: a packet may wait behind its controller's own earlier packets, and from the head of its own queue a controller with k lower target addresses
waits up to (N − 1 + k) transfers, because if its next packet arrives while it defers, the lower addresses may send before and after the idle window (C: 80.0 ms
Policy 4: nobody starves and the address no longer decides who waits longest, but every STOP is a lottery among the waiting controllers: worst 140 ms = 7.01 Tmax in
S1 and 26.2 ms in S2 (policy 3: 40.0 and 4.01 ms), 47.7 ms in S3 and 408 ms in S4. The bus stays idle after every STOP until the first probe, so the mean over all
packets is higher than with policies 1 and 3: 3.50 ms in S3 (policies 1 and 3: 3.27 and 3.28 ms); 30.8 ms in S4 (policies 1 and 3: 30.6 and 30.6 ms).
